h1: Process safety and permit control for oil and gas operations

problem.title: Why oil and gas safety needs more than a general EHS tool
problem.intro: Oil and gas operations combine major accident hazards, flammable and toxic inventories and large contractor workforces, often at sites hours from the nearest office or hospital.

points.title: Process safety and SIMOPS
points.text: Loss of containment, hot work in classified hazardous areas and simultaneous drilling, production and maintenance require permits, isolations and MOC to be checked against each other, not managed in silos.

points.title: H2S and toxic exposure
points.text: Sour gas fields and refinery units need gas test records, personal monitor data, H2S training status and rescue readiness verified before people enter the work area.

points.title: Turnarounds and remote sites
points.text: During shutdowns contractor headcount can multiply overnight, while offshore and desert sites run with little connectivity, making paper inductions, permits and competency checks the weak point.

features_title: How TECH EHS supports oil and gas operators
features_intro: Configured around the way upstream, midstream and downstream sites actually run: by asset, unit, area classification and contractor.

features.title: Integrated permits and isolations
features.text: Hot work, confined space, line break and electrical permits linked to isolation certificates, gas tests and hazardous area classification.

features.title: SIMOPS and area conflict checks
features.text: Flag incompatible activities by unit, module or well pad, such as hot work near a well intervention or lifting over live process equipment.

features.title: Process safety event tracking
features.text: Classify loss of primary containment events as Tier 1 to Tier 4 under API RP 754 and IOGP 456, with severity calculation and barrier analysis.

features.title: MOC and PSSR
features.text: Run management of change and pre-startup safety review workflows that meet OSHA PSM elements before any modified equipment returns to service.

features.title: Contractor and turnaround control
features.text: Pre-qualify contractor companies, verify individual competencies and inductions, and manage gate access during peak turnaround headcount.

features.title: Offline mobile for remote assets
features.text: Capture permits, inspections, observations and incidents offshore or in the desert without signal, and sync when the link is restored.

faqs.q: Does TECH EHS support OSHA PSM compliance?
faqs.a: Yes. Modules for MOC, PSSR, incident investigation, operating procedures, contractor management, training and audits map to the elements of OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 and similar process safety regulations.

faqs.q: Can process safety events be classified under API RP 754?
faqs.a: Yes. Loss of primary containment events are classified as Tier 1 to Tier 4 using API RP 754 and IOGP 456 thresholds for material release, consequence and location, and reported as rates by asset.

faqs.q: How does the system handle SIMOPS?
faqs.a: Permits and planned activities are tied to areas or equipment, and configurable rules flag incompatible combinations such as hot work during well intervention or crane lifts over pressurized lines, before approval.

faqs.q: Does the mobile app work offshore without connectivity?
faqs.a: Yes. The Android and iOS apps work fully offline for permits, inspections, observations and incidents, and synchronize when satellite or Wi-Fi connectivity is available.

faqs.q: Do you provide oil and gas training content too?
faqs.a: Yes. TECH EHS produces HSE e-learning and animated safety videos on topics such as H2S awareness, permit to work, confined space and incident recreation, in multiple languages.
